title: Concept card (.gamestudio/concepts/*.concept.json)
description: One game concept from ideation, scored for the concept tournament. All seven scores are oriented so that higher is better for us (production_cost 10 = cheapest), which lets tournaments sum or weight them directly. The winning concept seeds the design contract.

score.description: Score from 1 (worst) to 10 (best); halves allowed when averaging judges.

status.description: Tournament state: draft, shortlisted, winner (becomes the contract), parked (revisit later), killed (with rationale).

core_loop.description: Core loop as one line ("spawn -> merge -> defend -> earn") or as a loop graph.

hook.description: The novel twist that makes it worth making and easy to market in a 3-second ad.

scores.description: Rubric scores, each 1-10, higher is better. Unknown keys are rejected so a misspelt criterion cannot silently drop out of the ranking.

market.description: Market attractiveness: audience size, demand trend, competitive gap.

novelty.description: Freshness of the hook versus top-grossing and trending comparables.

fun_potential.description: Strength of the core loop as judged by paper or greybox prototype.

feasibility.description: Technical and design risk (10 = low risk).

monetization.description: Ethical revenue potential of the model and loops.

production_cost.description: Inverted cost: 10 = cheapest to produce (content volume, art complexity, team size).

agent_buildability.description: How well AI agents can build and verify it (deterministic sim, 2D, data-driven content, testable).

weighted_total.description: Optional computed weighted mean of the seven scores, 0-10.

risks.description: Key risks: strings, or risk objects as in the contract ({id, risk, likelihood, impact, mitigation}).

kill_criteria.description: Measurable conditions that would kill the concept (e.g. prototype fun score below 6 after two iterations).

rationale.description: Why this concept, why now, and why us; plus the judges' summary.
